acts.act_one: Opens in medias res at the climax with a two-minute ticking clock, then executes a double-rewind via unreliable voiceover—first to a false starting point (the support group), then to the true baseline (six months of insomnia and consumerist spiritual deadness). Establishes a temporary equilibrium where simulated mortality in support groups cures Jack's insomnia, which is disrupted when Marla arrives as a mirror-faker and restores his sleeplessness. The act culminates in a dual inciting incident: meeting Tyler on an airplane and the mysterious destruction of Jack's condo, followed by the threshold-crossing parking lot fistfight that moves Jack onto Paper Street.
acts.act_two: Structured as a gradual inversion of agency where therapeutic self-destruction mutates into institutional fascism. Early escalation expands the two-man fight into an underground network and blue-collar guerrilla pranks, complicated by a bizarre triangulation when Tyler saves and sleeps with Marla, alienating Jack in his own home. The midpoint hinges on a triple initiation into 'hitting bottom': the lye-burn ritual, the mock-execution of Raymond K. Hessel, and the intentional highway crash, interspersed with Jack blackmailing his boss via self-battery. In the second half, Tyler weaponizes the clubs into Project Mayhem (Space Monkeys), systematically excluding Jack. The low point strikes consecutively: Bob is killed by police during a sabotage run, and Jack's cross-country search triggers the twist that he and Tyler share a single body.
acts.act_three: Driven by a compressed race against an automated conspiracy that Jack himself engineered while 'asleep'. Every conventional avenue of resolution is structurally blocked because the infrastructure (bartenders, cabbies, police detectives) is already infiltrated and programmed by Tyler to treat Jack's warnings as a 'test'. The narrative loops back to the opening high-rise frame. In a physical and psychological climax intercut with objective security camera footage, Jack defeats his dissociative projection by shooting himself through the cheek—proving willingness to die to kill his 'god'. Resolves in an ironic synthesis: Tyler is gone and Marla is saved, but the bombs still detonate, leaving the fractured couple holding hands watching the financial skyline collapse.

mystery_hiding: Engineered through subjective third-person projection disguised as objective camera reality, governed by the structural mechanic that insomnia isActually fugue-state activity. The script hides the split personality in plain sight using strict spatial and conversational rules: Tyler and Marla are never seen in the same room together outside of closed-door sex; Tyler forces a three-time promise that Jack never speak of him to Marla; and in group scenes, only one of them speaks while the other observes silently. Foreshadowing is planted via shared physical markers (identical briefcases, identical lye-kiss scars, knowing recipes 'because Tyler knows this') and blocking mechanics (Jack beating himself up in his boss's office explicitly mirrors his first fight with Tyler). The reveal is triggered externally by a bruised bartender and confirmed by Marla over the phone, then visually proven by replaying key earlier scenes as 'altered flashbacks' where Jack occupies Tyler's space.
character_connections: Built on a psychological triad representing a single fractured psyche externalized into three poles: Jack (the repressed, passive ego), Tyler (the charismatic, nihilistic id/superego ideal), and Marla (the intrusive reality principle and emotional mirror). Marla and Tyler function as mutually exclusive poles—Marla's presence exposes Jack's lie, while Tyler's presence shields him from it. The central power dynamic is a master-disciple inversion: Jack unconsciously creates Tyler to liberate himself from consumerist impotence, but Tyler progressively usurps control of their shared body, reducing Jack from co-founder to an ignored cog. Secondary characters (Bob, Ricky, Angel Face) serve as barometers of Jack's displacement, shifting loyalty from Jack's empathetic peer group to Tyler's faceless cult. Jack's arc requires integrating his capacity for action while destroying his need for Tyler, allowing him to finally connect directly with Marla.
spine: An alienated, hollow man invents an idealized, hyper-masculine alter ego to escape consumerist numbness, only to have to destroy that creation when his pursuit of radical freedom mutates into totalitarian self-erasure.
key_structural_decisions: In medias res bookending with a false-start nested flashback: opening at two minutes to demolition, rewinding to Bob's embrace, and pausing again to rewind further to the insomnia origin, establishing narrative unreliability and structural control from page one.

Direct-address fourth-wall breaches and meta-cinematic framing: freezing the narrative at the tavern to introduce Tyler's night jobs direct-to-camera, and closing the script by catching the film strip itself in the projector gate with a spliced subliminal frame.

Escalation via parallel rhythmic montages: measuring the growth of the fight club through four identical zooming-out parking lot shots (6, 10, 14, 18 men) intercut with domestic decay on Paper Street, and later compressing the transition from individual applicant to cult army through the three-day porch initiation sequence.

Dual-perspective cross-cutting during the climax: intercutting Jack's subjective struggle against Tyler in the high-rise hallways with objective Security Camera POVs showing Jack shooting and wrestling himself alone.

Pre-programmed narrative dead-ends in Act Three: structuring Tyler's orders so that every subordinate and police officer interprets Jack's frantic attempts to abort the mission as a pre-planned loyalty test ('You told me you'd say that, Sir').
scene_rhythm: Propulsive, jagged alternation between rapid-fire, associative voiceover montages (IKEA catalog pop-ins, single-serving airport transitions, support group tours) and sustained, high-tension dramatic set-pieces (the convenience store gunpoint interrogation, the lye chemical burn, the boss's office self-beating, the highway crash). Scenes cut early on punchlines or thematic button lines, using overlapping dialogue and temporal intercutting (such as the biohazard fat heist intercut directly with the kitchen rendering lesson) to maintain relentless forward momentum.
